findings.claim: Default pipeline resolution selects a non-default pipeline when multiple active pipelines exist.
findings.evidence: defaultPipelineId orders by asc(isDefault) and takes one row. PostgreSQL sorts false before true, so unqualified lead creation and default-pipeline operations select a custom pipeline instead of the configured default.
findings.suggestion: Order isDefault descending, retaining the remaining fallback ordering. Cover a tenant with both default and non-default active pipelines.

findings.claim: Restoring a stage that was migrated or created while archived leaves it disconnected.
findings.evidence: Migration and creation generate transitions only for active stages. updateLeadStage restores status without creating any transitions. The in-memory planner probe confirmed that an archived stage receives zero edges. After restoration, moves into or out of that stage return transition_not_allowed, including for existing leads parked there.
findings.suggestion: Establish appropriate incident transitions when restoring a previously disconnected stage, while preserving configured graphs. Cover migration of an archived stage followed by restoration and movement.

findings.claim: Undoing an edit to a legacy contactless lead always fails.
findings.evidence: The real leadToWriteSeed function emits contactPhone:null and contactEmail:null. lead-service.ts:1125-1128 rejects PATCH requests touching contact fields when both remain empty. Normal editing explicitly omits these keys for legacy contactless leads, so editing a name succeeds but Desfazer receives contact_required.
findings.suggestion: Preserve contact-key omission when undoing an edit that left a legacy lead contactless, and verify the undo payload against the API contract.

findings.claim: An assigned follow-up owner can see their task but cannot complete it when another seller owns the lead.
findings.evidence: addLeadFollowup accepts another tenant person's ownerPersonId, and listFollowups includes tasks owned by the caller. markFollowupDone instead checks the lead's seller. A task assigned to Bruno on Ana's lead therefore appears in Bruno's Minha list but completion returns 404. Lead reassignment can produce the same mismatch.
findings.suggestion: Reconcile assignment, listing and completion authorization so task ownership has consistent behavior while preserving tenant and lead-access boundaries.

findings.claim: The board offers undo for stage moves whose reverse transition is forbidden.
findings.evidence: moveWithUndo publishes an inverse move for every non-conversion movement without checking the reverse edge. The actual transition planner allows normal-to-Perdido but creates no Perdido-to-normal edge. Consequently, moving a lead to Perdido succeeds and offers Desfazer, but clicking it receives 409 transition_not_allowed.
findings.suggestion: Only offer inverse movement when the graph permits it, or implement an explicitly authorized server-side undo operation. Cover terminal and asymmetric transitions.

checks.summary: Confirmed the review scope: 158 changed files.

Evaluated actual leadToWriteSeed and planPipelineTransitions functions. Confirmed null contact undo payload, missing archived-stage edges, and allowed forward movement with forbidden reverse movement. No files written.
Confirmed the mismatch between follow-up listing ownership and completion authorization.
Referenced schema file was absent; response follows the supplied strict output schema.
